newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Rates move hits dollar but Euro stocks up.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Rates move hits dollar but Euro stocks up.

text.p: The surprise U.S. decision not to raise interest rates left the dollar weaker on Wednesday but European bourses moved ahead cautiously in early trading.

Stocks in London, Frankfurt and Paris made a healthy start -- with German shares hitting a new peak -- shrugging off a 20-point overnight drop in Wall Street after the U.S. decision not to tighten credit.

But the dollar slipped by about 0.75 pfennigs, hit by the policy-making Federal Open Market Committee's decision to leave rates unchanged, catching out a market which had priced in a 0.25 percent rise.

Analysts said the move was a calculated gamble that the U.S. economy will slow before inflation starts to rise. But it disappointed forex markerts where higher rates would have made dollar-based assets more attractive to investors.
"The Fed's taking a risk and the dollar's vulnerable to any sort of strong data or any pick-up in inflation," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ in London.
The Fed's inaction had many market watchers concerned that a reluctance to increase rates ahead of the U.S. elections had influenced its decision.

Dealers said the dollar looked fragile in the near-term. "As incoming data provides further evidence that the economy is decelerating, starting with durable goods tomorrow, the market will need to reconsider whether the Fed will still tighten this year," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell here.
"Such a reassessment could yet exert greater pressure on the dollar," he added.

European equities looked much healthier. In Frankfurt, stocks on the DAX index hit a trading record of 2654.57 points in early transactions, eclipsing the previous high of 2650.49 set on September 20.
German shares initially weakened on profit-taking but the current bull-run quickly regained momentum, supported by stronger government bonds, dealers say.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, climbed by 0.3 percent but the mood was tense and traders said the gains were likely to be limited unless Wall Street rebounds from Tuesday's decline.
"There's a bit of disappointment out there that the Fed didn't go ahead with raising rates by 25 basis points. Everyone knows that they're going to raise rates eventually," said one trader.
"I don't think this market is going to get too carried away on the upside."
Paris shares also did well at the start climbing 0.7 percent to 2095 points but the bourse's advance ran into resistance as the CAC index neared the 2,100 mark.
"It looks like the Fed's move gives the bourse a month and a half of breathing space," until after the U.S. presidential election, a trader said.

Traders said the market was holding up well, with demand emerging at every dip, but they said investors were carefully watching Wall Street's reactions, the dollar's level and news about the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5064 marks and 109.85 yen compared with 1.5131 marks and 109.79 yen in Europe late on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 13.0 points up at 3,923.5.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 14.37 points up at 2,095.87.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 14.75 at 2,653.20. PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened at $382.90 an ounce compared to the London closing of $382.05. Silver was at $4.93, up four cents.
